I've been working this land for 45 years. I know this soil, I know this climate. My father farmed before me, and I learned by watching and doing, not from books. My wife and I manage everything ourselves now — the children are in the city. At my age, I have to be smart about what I take on.

My 15 mu breaks into two pieces: 10 mu I rotate between wheat and maize, and 5 mu I keep in cotton for cash. Cotton is hard work at harvest time, but I've always grown it and I know how to handle it. I won't expand it — my back isn't what it was.

For **wheat**, I plant in October after I rotary-till the field. I'll use the improved certified seed from the county supply store, same type I've used the last several years. I water it three times: once after planting to help it establish before the cold, once at jointing in spring, once at heading. I put down base fertilizer before planting and top-dress urea in spring. I spray twice — once for weeds early on, once for aphids and disease in April. I expect around 420 jin per mu.

After wheat harvest in June, I go straight into **maize** on the same land without plowing — I just direct-seed the hybrids into the stubble. Less work, and it gets the maize in fast. Zhengdan 958 or similar, whatever the seed shop recommends that year. I water twice — once to get it up, once during grain fill if it's dry. Two sprays for pests. I get 550 jin per mu most years.

For **cotton**, I plow in spring and plant in late April. I use hybrid Bt seed now — it really does reduce the worm pressure compared to the old days. Cotton drinks water and needs feeding. I water four times through the season, spray five times for pests and disease, and apply more potassium than for the grain crops because cotton needs it.
